findings.rule: spec.md Determinism: "tag headings ordered alphabetically by normalised class" (the first tag only) — doubt stated: the owner's own PR #132 review (item 9) already named this exact wording gap and marked it optional for the 0.3.7 tag.
findings.summary: The new sentence says the generated index carries "a heading per tag", but `plugin/lessons/index.py` groups only by the first tag (`tags[0]`), so a lesson with several tags gets one heading, not one per tag; a reader could expect the opposite.

findings.rule: doubt stated: narrow edge case — step 0b's instructions only ever write `supersedes` as a bare file name or omit it, so this path is unlikely to be hit in practice.
findings.summary: `_supersedes_problem` only validates `supersedes` when its value is already a string (`isinstance(supersedes, str)`); a present-but-non-string value (a list or a number) returns `None` and is silently treated as "no supersedes" instead of being reported as malformed.

findings.rule: doubt stated: cosmetic breakage of a generated markdown file, not a functional break — `/sdlc-maintain` matches lessons by heading/tags, not by parsing the link text.
findings.summary: `_render_line`/`_render_unsorted_line` interpolate `title`, `description` and the first heading into a markdown link (`[text](file)`) with no escaping of `]`/`(`/`)`, so a value containing one of those characters breaks the generated link in `lessons/index.md`.

findings.rule: doubt stated: a harmless side effect (an empty directory), not data loss or a wrong result; the owner's own PR #132 review (item 7) already named this and marked it optional for the 0.3.7 tag.
findings.summary: `build()` unconditionally runs `lessons_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`, so the read-only `check()` (and `lesson_and_eval`'s call into it) creates `lessons/` as a side effect on a project that has none yet, e.g. when no lesson file matches the gate's glob at all.

The example frontmatter's `sources` list shows only `detection`, `eval` and `fix-pr`, with no sample `run-<n>` entry, even though spec.md's Requirements say `sources` includes "one `run-<n>` per failed run `detection.json` lists".
